Six rooms

A channel is not one fixed ritual. Pick a room, then assemble its cast, session routes, shared entities, and durable message shape.

01Build the room

All six examples use the same graph laws. What changes is the roster, which teammate sessions should receive a top-level message, and where discussion branches.

        03What the product does today

        solid ink · verified
        • A channel is a graph entity with a feed, composer, threaded branches, pinned entities, and nested subchannels.
        • has_member connects a channel to members and teammates. It is a roster, not an ACL or subscription.
        • A top-level @ teammate tag reuses a live work session or starts one, then stores one message across the channel and addressed session anchors.
        • Tasks and docs selected in the attach picker are extra message anchors, so the same message also appears in their Discussion.
        • Messages are stored first. A finished session can retain a message without being woken; live delivery is a separate outcome.
        ghost ink · boundary

        Text rooms only

        The live CLI exposes grants for voice_channel entities, but this build check did not establish a dedicated voice-room component in the current UI source. These six examples do not imply a working voice-room experience.

        Also: session and teammate @ actions are top-level channel actions. Thread replies do not spawn or address sessions.
